title: Breaking the Benchmark: Revealing LLM Bias via Minimal Contextual Augmentation
findings: For the religion bias category, contextual and question augmentation significantly increased the rate of 'Decisive Responses' (potentially biased answers in ambiguous contexts) from 25.95% in the original format to 56.72% in the fully augmented format. This reveals that models which appear fair on standard benchmarks may harbor latent biases that surface under semantic perturbations, suggesting they overfit to benchmark formats rather than internalizing fairness principles.
